heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a split hero with the copy locked left and a layered production-style media composition on the right: a dark AI workstation mockup, orange-lit model cards, output thumbnails, prompt chips, and waveform strips. Keep the overall feel engineered and enterprise-grade, with orange as the dominant brand signal and subtle motion only on UI layers. No autoplay video; show the video capability through a preview card within the composite.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses a split text-plus-visual composition with orange-dominant background
Trust is intentionally compressed and de-emphasized because no logos or counts are available
Seedream is presented as a spotlight-led product module with a capability grid
Seedance switches to a contrastive accordion-style module to avoid repeating the same visual pattern
Testimonials are handled as a carousel to reduce vertical bloat and add motion
Pricing uses a comparison-led card treatment instead of another feature grid
Form is isolated as a floating conversion card to close with a distinct rhythm
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Seedream 4.5 for high-fidelity AI image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for synchronized AI video creation with ByteDance generative models.

sections.backgroundTreatment: orange-dominant split canvas with dark interface overlays and precision-line detailing
sections.designNote: Make the hero content-first, but visually dynamic. Left side carries the long headline, concise enterprise value proposition, and primary CTA. Right side should show an orange-lit AI workstation mockup with layered image and video generation panels, prompt chips, output thumbnails, and inference timeline strips. Keep the composition dense and premium rather than airy.

Trust is minimal because no logos, counts, or badges are available. Use a restrained utility row that can hold model credibility markers, enterprise readiness cues, and lightweight proof language without overpowering the hero.

Use two product blocks with alternating structure and strong contrast. Seedream 4.5 should lead with a spotlight-plus-grid feel for image generation, emphasizing text-image alignment, 4K fidelity, typography, composition, and structural control. Seedance 1.5 Pro should shift into an accordion-with-visual layout so the audio-visual synchronization, multilingual lip-sync, cinematic camera control, and speed advantages feel more technical and differentiated. The product area should not read like generic SaaS cards; it should feel like two engineered capability modules.

If included, keep this as a brief confidence section rather than a marketing block. Use a compact grid of practical reasons to buy through the platform, but keep emphasis low because the content map does not provide a full proof system.

Present pricing as an enterprise-oriented comparison summary rather than a loud price wall. Seedance can carry the visible starting price, while Seedream should feel quote-led and value-heavy. Keep cards sharp, technical, and restrained, with the CTA anchored in procurement language like Get Quote.

Use a testimonial carousel because there are 4+ testimonials. Keep the slides dark, compact, and professional, with roles like Creative Director, Video Producer, Art Director, Marketing Manager, and Creative Lead. This should read as proof-led credibility, not a fluffy social section.

End with a high-contrast conversion card floating over the orange brand field. The form should feel decisive and minimal, using the primary CTA language from the hero. Keep the structure short and enterprise-oriented so the page ends on a clear action rather than another content block.
Only use this if needed for footer-adjacent utility. Since no media or news sources are supplied, keep it as a subtle placeholder strip or omit visually dominant treatment.

blueprint.designPersonality: Engineered creative intelligence — dark, precise, premium, and enterprise-ready, with orange as the unmistakable brand signal and modular layouts that make ByteDance’s generative models feel fast, capable, and serious.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a high-contrast dark UI mockup style with orange-lit model shells, floating output thumbnails, waveform strips, prompt chips, and technical inference overlays. The hero visual should feel like a production AI workstation: layered panels, generation timelines, and result previews for image and video. Avoid playful illustrations; use sleek abstract product visuals, PNG UI composites, and one large JPEG hero composition with subtle glow accents.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so the size is reduced to keep it clean and avoid wrap fatigue while still feeling commanding.

colours.colourReason: The brand’s primary orange must drive the hero background and primary CTA. Dark charcoal and black support the required dark theme, while muted greys maintain premium contrast. No generic purple or blue palette is used.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width top banner with a left-aligned brand/logo area, large headline stack, short supporting copy, and a compact benefit list; no evidence of split media hero or carousel in the active markup. The hero reads as a dense promotional intro with strong vertical hierarchy and immediate lead capture below.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single prominent hero followed by a lead form section; rhythm is section-by-section rather than card-grid storytelling. Content appears front-loaded, with minimal intermediate modules and strong contrast between promotional header and conversion form.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Form card and content blocks use simple rectangular containers with functional, utility-first presentation. No glassmorphism, no elevated editorial cards, and no complex shadow treatment is evident from the provided HTML.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion is driven by a single dominant action in the hero and a secondary lead-generation form below. CTA strategy is direct and utility-oriented, with limited visible hierarchy beyond one main action and a form submission path.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module is present in the provided reference markup, so no reusable pricing pattern can be extracted from this page.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in the provided HTML excerpt; no reusable footer pattern extracted.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Light media usage centered on logo and small inline iconography within the hero list; no large product imagery, no video panel, and no background media pattern evident.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: No dedicated product detail sections are visible in the excerpt beyond the hero and form; the page relies on a lead-gen landing structure rather than multi-section product education.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead form appears as a dedicated conversion block directly after the hero, likely within a bordered card. Pattern is stacked, high-priority, and designed for data capture rather than exploration; hidden fields indicate routed attribution and campaign tracking.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation system is visible in the provided markup; any motion appears limited to optional slider scaffolding in commented code rather than active page behavior.
componentPatterns: Large hero headline and supporting paragraph
designNotes: Structure is optimized for enterprise lead generation.
Strong above-the-fold messaging with immediate conversion intent.
Use compact bullet benefits to reduce reading friction.
Keep layout utilitarian and form-forward rather than content-rich.
Commented carousel code suggests the system may support alternate banner variants, but the active page is static.

mustHaveMoments: Clear hero message that explains both Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro in one glance
Fast credibility through testimonial snippets from creative and marketing roles
Dedicated product differentiation blocks for image generation and video generation
Simple pricing/quote path with quote-oriented CTAs
Strong dark-theme visual treatment with premium AI/enterprise cues
avoidPatterns: Split-screen hero with heavy media that distracts from the core value proposition
Overly airy editorial layout that delays conversion points
Generic stock visuals or abstract AI imagery without product relevance
Multiple competing CTAs above the fold
Overly decorative glassmorphism or high-shadow card styling
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is best structured as a high-intent demo-booking experience for solution-aware buyers who already understand the AI content category and need confidence, clarity, and proof. Because the offering includes two related generative models, the narrative should stay product-led but use testimonials as the primary trust layer to validate use cases for creative, marketing, and video teams. A centered dark-theme hero should deliver a strong message-first introduction, followed quickly by dense but scannable product detail, benefits, and quote-oriented conversion moments. The design should feel futuristic and premium, but not overly experimental, so the user can evaluate capability and move into a demo or quote request with minimal friction.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
